Al-thālith: law talīnu fayalīnūn (if you would be soft, so they would be soft), qālahu al-Farrāʾ.

Al-rābiʿ: law takdhibu fayakdhibūn (if you would lie, so they would lie), qālahu al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas.

Al-sādis: an tadhhaba ʿan hādhā al-amr fayadhhabūna maʿaka (that you would turn away from this matter, so they would go with you), qālahu Qatādah.

Aḥaduhumā: mujāmalat al-ʿaduww wa-mumāyalatuhu (courtesy toward and leaning toward the enemy). Qāla al-shāʿir:

﻿؎ Labaʿḍu al-ghashm aḥzamu umūrin tanūbuka min mudāhanati al-ʿaduww.

Al-thānī: annahā al-nifāq (hypocrisy) wa-tark al-munāṣahah (abandoning sincere counsel), qālahu al-Mufaḍḍal. Fahiya ʿalā hādhā al-wajh madhmūmah, wa-ʿalā al-wajh al-awwal ghayru madhmūmah.

Aḥaduhā: annahu al-kadhdhāb (the liar), qālahu Ibn ʿAbbās.

Al-thālith: annahu al-mikthār min al-sharr (one who abounds in evil), qālahu Qatādah.

Al-rābiʿ: annahu al-dhalīl bil-bāṭil (one debased by falsehood), qālahu Ibn Shajarah.

﻿؎ Tudlī bi-wuddin idhā lāqaytanī kadhiban ∗∗∗ wa-in aghību fa-anta al-hāmiz al-lumazah.

Aḥaduhumā: annahumā lughatān (they are two dialects), qālahu al-Farrāʾ.

Al-thālith: annahu al-wafīr al-jism (large of body), qālahu al-Ḥasan and Abū Razīn.

Al-thānī: annahu al-ẓalūm (the wrongdoer), qālahu Ibn ʿAbbās fī riwāyat Ibn Ṭalḥah ʿanhu.

Al-sādis: annahu al-daʿiyy (the one claimed by others, adopted falsely). Qāla al-shāʿir:

﻿؎ Zanīmun tadāʿāhu al-rijālu ziyādatan ∗∗∗ kamā zīda fī ʿarḍi al-adīmi al-akāriʿu.

Al-thāmin: annahu ʿalāmatu al-kufr, kamā qāla taʿālā: ﴿سَنَسِمُهُ عَلى الخُرْطُومِ﴾ [We will brand him upon the snout], qālahu Abū Razīn.

﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾. It is said that this garden was a plantation in Yemen, in a village called Dhawaran, between which and Sana'a of Yemen was a distance of twelve miles. Regarding it there are two opinions:

The first: it belonged to a people from Abyssinia.

The second, said by Qatadah: it belonged to an old man from the Children of Israel who had sons. He would keep from its produce what was sufficient for himself and his family, and give away the rest in charity. His sons began to reproach him and said: "If we were in charge of it, we would certainly act differently." He would not obey them until he died, and they inherited it. They said: "We are more in need, due to the large number of our dependents, than the poor and the needy." ﴿So they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾, meaning they swore that they would cut its fruit when they woke in the morning.

The first: they did not make an exception for the needy. Said by Ikrimah.

The second: their exception was the saying "Glory be to our Lord." Said by Abu Salih.

The third: the saying "If God wills."

﴿Then a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep﴾. Regarding this there are three meanings:

The first: a command from your Lord. Said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: a punishment from your Lord. Said by Qatadah.

The third: that it was a flame of fire that came out from the valley of their garden. Said by Ibn Juraij.

﴿While they were asleep﴾, meaning at night, at the time of sleep. Al-Farra' said: the visitation occurs only at night.

The first: like black ash. Said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: like the dark night. Said by al-Farra'. The poet said:

The third: like a harvest that has been cut, in which no fruit remains.

Aswat related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of sins, for a servant commits a sin and is thereby deprived of a provision that had been prepared for him." ﴿So they called to one another in the morning﴾, meaning some of them called out to others at dawn.

﴿Go out early to your field﴾. Mujahid said: the field was grapes.

﴿If you are going to harvest﴾, meaning determined to cut your produce on this day.

﴿So they set off while whispering to one another﴾. Regarding this there are four meanings:

The first: they were speaking. Said by Ikrimah.

The second: they concealed their speech and kept it secret, so that no one would learn of them. Said by Ata' and Qatadah.

The third: they hid themselves from the people so that they would not be seen.

The fourth: they were not consulting among themselves.

﴿That no needy person will enter it today against you﴾. Said by Yahya ibn Salam.

﴿And they set off early, [resolved] with determination﴾. Regarding this there are nine meanings:

The first: with anger. Said by Ikrimah.

The second: with diligence. Said by Mujahid.

The third: with withholding. Said by Abu 'Ubaydah.

The fourth: with intent. From this is the saying of the poet:

"A torrent came from God's presence, / rushing with the rush of the well-stocked garden."

That is, it aimed for the aim of the well-stocked garden.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 68, verses 34–41:

﴿Am lakum aymanun ʿalaynā bālighah﴾ — "Or do you have oaths upon Us, binding until the Day of Resurrection?" Al-bālighah means emphasized by (an oath in) Allah.

﴿Inna lakum lamā taḥkumūn﴾ — "Indeed, for you is whatever you judge." In it there are two interpretations:

The first: "Or do you have oaths upon Us, binding, that We will not punish you in this world until the Day of Resurrection?"

﴿Salhum ayyuhum bidhālika zaʿīm﴾ — "Ask them, which of them stands surety for that?" In it there are two interpretations:

The first: that the zaʿīm (guarantor, surety) is the kafīl (sponsor, guarantor). This is related from Ibn ʿAbbās.

The second: that it is the Messenger. This is related from al-Ḥasan.

And it may admit a third: that it is the one entrusted with the affair, because of his precedence and leadership.

> *"They uncovered for them its shin, and there appeared from evil its unmixed harm."*

> *"The war has uncovered its shin, so tie up your bonds, and the war has urged you on, so strive."*

Third: "We seize them from where they step and crawl." This is the view of Ibn Bahr.
